events.text: I'll search for the latest versions of all cited studies simultaneously.

Now I have enough information to assess all eight cited studies. Let me also check whether the Shojania 2009 Cochrane review (source [7]) has ever been updated, and whether the Ames 2019 qualitative synthesis has been updated, using what I already found.

From the searches:
- **[1] Agarwal 2025** (CD012925.pub2): Confirmed as published 7 April 2025 — this IS the latest version. CURRENT.
- **[2] Agarwal 2021** (CD012944.pub2): Last version published 27 July 2021. No update found. UNKNOWN (cannot positively confirm no update exists, but no newer version found).
- **[3] Palmer 2020** (CD013679): Published 2020 Issue 8. No update found. UNKNOWN.
- **[4] Ames 2019** (CD013447): Published 14 October 2019. No update found. UNKNOWN.
- **[5] WHO 2019 guideline**: The 2019 guideline (WHO/RHR/19.8) appears to remain the current version; a WHO digital health products document references a "2nd ed" completed May 2024, but this appears to be a classification document, not the recommendations guideline itself. UNKNOWN — cannot positively confirm the 2019 guideline has not been superseded.
- **[6] Arditi 2017** (CD001175.pub4): The 2017 version is pub4 (updated from pub3 in 2012). No newer version found. UNKNOWN.
- **[7] Shojania 2009** (CD001096.pub2): Published 2009. No update found. This is a 17-year-old review. UNKNOWN — and notably old.
- **[8] Derksen 2025** (Implementation Science 2025;20:33, published 17 July 2025): Confirmed current. A sub-analysis (BJGP 2026) cites it as the parent review. CURRENT.

I found no grounds to object to the other sentences:

- The patient-outcomes sentences match the review: certainty is very low, from 6 studies and seven comparisons.
- The heterogeneity quotation is accurate.
- The harms sentence is a fair reading. The review says none of the included studies reported outcomes related to harms or adverse effects, such as redundant testing or overdiagnosis.

I found no sentence on the page that my document contradicts. Every figure and characterisation I checked matches the review. These are the median of 4.2% (IQR 0.8% to 18.8%) and the clinical endpoint median of 2.5% (IQR 1.3% to 4.2%). The 5.6% best-outcome figure and the "small to modest" wording also match. I confirmed these against the abstract and main text as indexed on Cochrane, PubMed and PMC. I did not separately check the blood pressure figure (1.0 mmHg) or the 6.2% medication best-outcome figure in the full text. I found no omitted finding that would change the page's conclusions, so I returned only the two minor omissions above.
